paper.title: Space Physics: exam practice
paper.instructions: Exam practice for one topic: about 25 minutes. You may use a calculator. Answer all the questions. Use g = 9.8 N/kg. Equations you are not expected to remember are given in the question. Show your working in calculations: you can get marks for method even if your final answer is wrong. Questions marked 6 marks are extended answers: write in full sentences and organise your ideas.

questions.question_text:
Explain how observations of light from distant galaxies support the Big Bang theory, and what more recent observations suggest about the universe.

(6 marks)

levels.descriptor: A clear explanation of red-shift, how it shows the universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang, plus the more recent evidence from supernovae and what it suggests.
Some explanation of red-shift and how it supports the Big Bang, possibly without the more recent observations.
Simple statements about galaxies, red-shift or the Big Bang.

indicative: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted: its wavelength is longer than expected
This means the galaxies are moving away from us
The further away a galaxy is, the greater its red-shift, so the faster it is moving away
So the whole universe is expanding
If it is expanding, it must once have been much smaller: it began from a very small, extremely hot and dense region (the Big Bang)
Since 1998, observations of supernovae suggest that distant galaxies are moving away faster and faster: the expansion is accelerating
Scientists suggest this is caused by dark energy, and there may be dark mass too
These are not yet understood, so the theory may change as new evidence is found
scheme.guidance: Level 3 needs red-shift linked to expansion and the Big Bang, and at least one more recent observation.

questions.subtopic: The solar system and the life cycle of a star
questions.question_text:
This question is about stars.

(a) Name the force that pulls clouds of dust and gas together to form a star. (1 mark)

(b) Explain what has to happen inside a protostar for it to become a main sequence star. (2 marks)

(c) Describe what will eventually happen to the Sun after its main sequence stage. (2 marks)

(d) Elements heavier than iron are found on Earth. Explain how they got here. (2 marks)

points: (b) The temperature and pressure in the core become high enough
(b) For hydrogen nuclei to fuse to form helium (nuclear fusion starts)
(c) It will swell to become a red giant
(c) Then it will become a white dwarf (and eventually a black dwarf)
(d) Elements heavier than iron were made in a supernova (the explosion of a massive star)
(d) The supernova spread them through space, and our solar system formed from that material

questions.subtopic: Orbital motion, natural and artificial satellites
questions.question_text:
This question is about the solar system and orbits.

(a) Describe what makes up our solar system. (2 marks)

(b) Satellite A orbits 400 km above the Earth's surface. Satellite B orbits 36 000 km above it. Which satellite moves faster? Explain your answer. (2 marks)

(c) What force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun? (1 mark)

(d) Give one use of artificial satellites. (1 mark)

points: (a) One star (the Sun) and eight planets
(a) Dwarf planets (e.g. Pluto) and natural satellites (moons), plus asteroids and comets
(b) It is closer, where the gravitational force is stronger, so it must move faster to stay in a stable orbit
(c) Gravity (the gravitational attraction of the Sun)
(d) A valid use, e.g. communications, weather monitoring, satellite navigation (GPS), observing the Earth or space
